title: Color on a dashboard: thresholds, color schemes, and value mappings (preview)

blocks.content: Explore dashboards on Grafana Play to see where color changes, where a panel's color comes from, and where a word replaces a number.
Explore panels on Grafana Play to see where their color changes, which direction is bad, and how Absolute and Percentage thresholds differ.
Open **Sample Website Dashboard**.
Focus on the **Memory** gauge.
The color runs green, then orange from 200, then red from 270. Higher is worse.
Focus on the **Sign ups** stat.
The color runs red, then orange from 100, then green from 270. Higher is better.
Open **Threshold example**.
Focus on the **Threshold Example** panel.
This panel has five thresholds: red from the Base value, orange from 10, transparent from 20, orange from 60, and red from 80. The line and shaded areas show where each color applies.
Open the panel for editing.

steps.reftarget: div[data-viz-panel-key='panel-1'] button[data-testid='data-testid Panel menu Threshold Example']
steps.description: Click here to open the panel menu.
Click Edit to open the panel editor.

blocks.content: Expand **Thresholds** if it's collapsed.
Find **Thresholds mode**.

**Absolute** thresholds are defined by a number. For example, 80 on a scale of 1 to 150. **Percentage** thresholds are defined relative to the minimum or maximum. For example, 80 percent. This panel uses **Absolute**.
Leave the editor.

steps.description: Click Back to return to the dashboard.

steps.reftarget: button[data-testid='data-testid Exit edit mode button'], button[data-testid='data-testid Edit dashboard button']
steps.description: The dashboard is still in edit mode. Click Exit edit.

blocks.content: If Grafana asks about unsaved changes, select **Discard**. Nothing needed saving.
Explore the panels on Sample Website Dashboard to see which keep palette colors and which take their color from a threshold.

blocks.title: Where a panel's color comes from

blocks.content: Open **Sample Website Dashboard**.
Focus on the time series panels: **Memory / CPU**, **logins**, **server requests**, and **client side full page load**.
These panels use **Classic palette**, so Grafana assigns each series a color based on its order.
Focus on the **Memory** and **Google hits** gauges, the **Support calls** and **Sign ups** stats, and the **Google hits** bar gauge.
These panels use **From thresholds (by value)**, so each takes its color from the matching threshold.
Explore panels on Grafana Play to see where a value mapping shows a word in place of a value, and where the mapping's color shows.
Open **Time series graphs**.
Focus on the **Value mappings that work on y-axis** panel.

The values 0, 1, and 2 are mapped to the text NORM, WARN, and CRIT, so the y-axis shows words in place of numbers. On a time series, the mapping's colors aren't applied, but the text is shown on the axis.
Open **Table**.
Focus on the **Value mapped colors** panel.
The mapping gives each text value a color: LOW is blue, NORMAL is green, HIGH is orange, and CRITICAL is red.
Open **State timeline and Status history**.
Focus on the **Status history - boolean values** panel.
A **Special** mapping shows true as the text True in green and false as the text False in red.
